strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem: structured pruning of LLMs without downstream retraining, where direct parameter-count and memory reductions are valuable.
The proposed compensation step is simple and analytically motivated via the Orthogonal Procrustes problem, making the core method easy to understand and potentially easy to implement.

The paper includes useful ablations separating pruning score effects, least-squares versus rotation compensation, rotation-only versus rotation-plus-scale, and which projection modules receive the update.
Empirical results show consistent perplexity improvements over WANDA-sp and competitive or slightly better results than FLAP on the reported LLaMA-7B setting.
weaknesses: The novelty is limited. Orthogonal Procrustes alignment and geometry-preserving rotations are classical, and the variance-aware score is a small heuristic modification of activation-aware pruning scores. The distinction from related rotation-based pruning/reparameterization methods such as SliceGPT is asserted but not deeply analyzed.

The evaluation is too narrow for a top-tier AI paper. Experiments are only on LLaMA-7B, with no results on newer or differently structured models such as LLaMA-2/3, OPT, Mistral, or larger scales, and perplexity is reported only on WikiText-2.

Baseline coverage is incomplete. The paper compares mainly against WANDA-sp and FLAP, but does not include strong structured-pruning baselines such as SliceGPT-style methods, LLM-Pruner variants, ShortGPT/depth pruning where relevant, or combinations with more modern post-pruning recovery methods.

The reported gains are modest and sometimes inconsistent. On zero-shot benchmarks, improvements over FLAP are small, and at 30% pruning the rotation-only variant is worse than FLAP in mean accuracy; several individual tasks also favor baselines.

There is a possible calibration/evaluation concern: WikiText-2 is used for calibration and also for reported perplexity, but the paper does not clearly separate calibration samples from evaluation or report results on out-of-domain corpora such as C4/PTB.

Important implementation details are underspecified, including whether pruning and compensation are applied sequentially layer by layer using updated activations, how corresponding dimensions are removed across coupled transformer projections, and how numerical issues in the large SVD are handled.

The technical motivation is somewhat overclaimed. Preserving norms and inner products of a layer output after applying an orthogonal map does not by itself ensure preservation of the downstream model function, since downstream layers are not invariant to arbitrary rotations unless corresponding transformations are propagated or compensated.
Reproducibility is limited: no code, hyperparameter sensitivity, calibration-set sensitivity, random seed variance, confidence intervals, or detailed evaluation protocol choices are provided.

Efficiency claims are incomplete. The method requires a dense dout x dout SVD per treated sub-layer; the paper reports per-layer pruning time but does not compare end-to-end pruning cost against baselines or discuss memory/runtime bottlenecks for larger models.

The writing is generally understandable but has some grammatical issues and occasional overstatements, especially in interpreting benchmark task improvements and claiming comprehensive effectiveness from a limited experimental setting.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem: structured pruning of LLMs without downstream retraining, where direct reductions in parameter count and memory are useful for deployment.
The proposed use of Orthogonal Procrustes for post-pruning compensation is simple, analytically tractable, and easy to integrate into a layerwise pruning pipeline.
The variance-aware pruning score is intuitive and the paper includes ablations separating the effects of pruning score and compensation method.
The experiments report both perplexity and downstream zero-shot accuracy, and include some practical efficiency measurements such as model size and pruning time.
weaknesses: The technical motivation is not fully convincing. Rotating output coordinates preserves norms and inner products within the calibration outputs, but transformer representations are not invariant to arbitrary rotations at these locations, especially with residual connections, downstream fixed weights, and coordinate-dependent learned structure. The paper asserts geometry preservation as beneficial without adequately justifying why this is the right constraint for post-pruning LLM layers.

The empirical evaluation is too narrow for a top-tier venue. Results are shown only on LLaMA-7B, with only three pruning ratios and a small set of baselines. Important structured pruning comparisons such as SliceGPT-style methods, LLM-Pruner variants, and stronger recent compression baselines are not evaluated.

The gains are modest and inconsistent. On zero-shot tasks, RCPU often improves only slightly over FLAP or WANDA-sp and is worse on several individual benchmarks. At 30% pruning, the rotation-only variant is below FLAP in mean accuracy, and the scaled variant improves over FLAP by only a very small margin.

The paper overclaims based on limited evidence. Claims of consistent improvement and practical applicability are not well supported by the tables, since several task-level results are mixed and the method requires expensive full output-dimensional SVDs per treated sub-layer.

The formulation is underspecified relative to the actual structured pruning implementation. The manuscript says corresponding positions in other projection matrices are removed, and attention pruning is done at head level, but the exact structural transformations needed to keep the model executable are not described clearly enough for reproducibility.

The evaluation protocol lacks important details and safeguards. It is unclear whether WikiText-2 calibration and perplexity evaluation use disjoint splits, how calibration samples are selected, whether random variation is measured, and whether reported differences are statistically meaningful.

The method is compared against least-squares fitting but does not include stronger regularized alternatives such as ridge, low-rank adapters, diagonal/scaled transformations, or constrained updates that might address the same overfitting concern more directly.

The related work positioning is weak. The distinction from SliceGPT and other rotation/reparameterization-based pruning work is discussed briefly but not deeply enough, and the novelty appears incremental: Procrustes alignment after pruning plus a variance factor in an existing activation-aware score.

The complexity discussion is somewhat concerning. A per-layer SVD of a 4096-by-4096 matrix for LLaMA-7B may be manageable, but the paper does not convincingly analyze scaling to larger models, nor does it report total pruning time across all layers and submodules.

The writing contains several grammatical issues and imprecise statements, and the paper would benefit from a much clearer explanation of how the compact pruned model is represented and evaluated after column/head removal.

strengths: The paper proposes a clean and technically plausible post-pruning compensation method based on Orthogonal Procrustes alignment, with an intuitive geometry-preserving motivation.
The method is simple to insert after structured column pruning and does not require retraining or architectural changes beyond the pruning procedure.
Experiments show consistent perplexity improvements over Wanda-sp and FLAP on WikiText-2 across 10%, 20%, and 30% pruning ratios.
The paper includes useful ablations comparing no compensation, least-squares compensation, rotation compensation, and different compensation targets, which support the central design choice.
The efficiency analysis reports concrete parameter, memory, and pruning-time numbers, helping establish practical relevance.
weaknesses: Novelty is moderate: Orthogonal Procrustes alignment is classical, and orthogonal rotations have already appeared in LLM compression contexts such as SliceGPT; the distinction is explained but the conceptual advance remains somewhat incremental.
The empirical evaluation is narrow for a top-tier AI venue: only LLaMA-7B is studied, with no larger models, no newer model families, and no cross-model robustness analysis.
Baselines are limited. The paper compares mainly against Wanda-sp and FLAP, but stronger or more directly competitive structured pruning/compression methods are not comprehensively evaluated.

Downstream accuracy gains are small and somewhat mixed. Mean improvements over FLAP are marginal at several pruning ratios, and RCPU is worse on some individual tasks, making the practical impact less decisive than the perplexity results suggest.
The paper would benefit from stronger statistical reporting, including multiple calibration samples/seeds, variance estimates, and significance or robustness analysis.
Some claims are stronger than the evidence, especially around preserving pretrained geometry and avoiding overfitting; these are plausible but not directly measured beyond downstream metrics.
Reproducibility details are incomplete: implementation specifics for pruning coupled dimensions, calibration preprocessing, evaluation settings, and code availability are not sufficiently described.
The computational cost of a full output-dimensional SVD per treated layer may be nontrivial for larger models, but scalability beyond 7B is not experimentally demonstrated.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem: training-free structured pruning of LLMs, where actual parameter-count and memory reductions are more deployable than unstructured sparsity on generic hardware.

The core method is simple and appealing: after column pruning, compensate the retained subspace via a closed-form Orthogonal Procrustes update, optionally with global scaling. This gives a clear geometric interpretation and avoids tuning a ridge regularization parameter.
The variance-aware pruning score is easy to implement and naturally complements the rotation-based compensation by trying to preserve high-variation directions before alignment.

Experiments cover multiple pruning ratios, two main base models, an additional Vicuna appendix, perplexity, and several zero-shot benchmarks. The method generally improves over Wanda-sp and FLAP, especially at higher pruning levels.

The paper includes useful ablations comparing no compensation, least-squares/ridge compensation, rotation compensation, scaling, and different compensation targets, which helps support the main design choices.
weaknesses: Novelty is moderate. Orthogonal Procrustes alignment, activation-aware pruning scores, and post-pruning compensation are all well-established ingredients; the contribution is a relatively straightforward recombination rather than a major new pruning principle.

The experimental comparison is not strong enough for a top-tier claim. Baselines are limited, SliceGPT is only partially evaluated, and several relevant structured LLM pruning or rotation/pruning methods are not compared directly under a unified protocol.

The evaluation is narrow for deployment claims. It uses mostly Llama-7B/Llama-2-13B with WikiText-2 calibration and evaluation plus standard zero-shot tasks, but lacks larger models, newer model families, realistic latency/throughput measurements, hardware-specific speedups, or generation-quality evaluations.

There is a possible calibration/evaluation concern: WikiText-2 is used for calibration and also for perplexity reporting, but the split/protocol is not sufficiently explicit. This weakens the interpretation of perplexity gains as generalization rather than calibration-set adaptation.

The paper reports parameter count and memory size, but not end-to-end inference latency, tokens/sec, or actual memory behavior in a deployed compact implementation. For structured pruning, these measurements are central to the practical value proposition.

The theoretical justification is somewhat informal. The paper argues that rotations preserve geometry and reduce overfitting, but does not provide a rigorous generalization analysis, and the degrees-of-freedom comparison to ridge regression is not fully convincing as evidence of robustness.

Ablations are still incomplete given the number of design choices. The paper does not sufficiently isolate the variance-aware score from the rotation update across all settings, study sensitivity to calibration distribution, or analyze per-layer pruning/compensation behavior in depth.

Reproducibility is weaker than expected: the footnote for code availability appears incomplete, implementation details for pruning coupled projections and head-level pruning are sparse, and there are no error bars or repeated-seed results.

Some claims are overstated. The method is described as practically applicable to large-scale deployment, but the SVD cost, dense rotation updates, compact-model implementation details, and real inference benefits are not demonstrated comprehensively.

strengths: The paper studies a relevant practical problem: training-free structured pruning of LLMs, where direct parameter-count reduction is more useful than unstructured sparsity for many deployment settings.
The proposed compensation step is simple and analytically tractable, using an Orthogonal Procrustes update rather than adding a complex optimization or retraining loop.
The experiments include perplexity and several zero-shot benchmarks across multiple pruning ratios, with some additional ablations on calibration size, compensation target, and LS/Ridge alternatives.
The method often improves perplexity over Wanda-sp and FLAP, especially at higher pruning ratios, suggesting that post-pruning compensation can be useful.
weaknesses: The novelty is limited. Orthogonal Procrustes alignment is a standard tool, and the paper does not convincingly distinguish the contribution from existing rotation-based pruning/reparameterization methods beyond applying a known closed-form alignment after pruning.

The central geometric claim is overstated. The rotation preserves the geometry of the pruned outputs Z, not necessarily the geometry of the original outputs Y, and the method cannot restore information removed by column pruning. The variance-aware score is only weakly motivated and not rigorously tied to preserving principal output directions.

The empirical gains are often small or inconsistent on downstream tasks. In several low-pruning settings RCPU is only marginally better than Wanda-sp/FLAP or not clearly superior on individual tasks, so the evidence does not support the strong claims of consistent superiority.

The evaluation is too narrow for a top-tier conference. It mainly uses Llama-7B, Llama-2-13B, and Vicuna-7B, with no modern Llama-3/Mistral-style models, no instruction-following or generation-quality evaluation, and no direct inference latency/throughput measurements despite deployment-oriented claims.

Baselines are incomplete and uneven. SliceGPT is only partially evaluated, several relevant structured pruning and rotation/pruning methods are missing, and comparisons to LS/Ridge depend on a questionable calibration-set hyperparameter selection protocol.

Ablations are insufficient. The paper does not cleanly isolate the contribution of the variance-aware scoring rule versus the rotation update in the main benchmark tables, nor does it provide enough evidence that the variance factor is better than simpler activation statistics.

Reproducibility is weak. The manuscript says code is available but leaves the code URL blank, and it lacks important details such as exact calibration sampling, harness settings, seeds, variance over runs, and implementation specifics for physically removing dimensions across connected projections.

Efficiency claims are under-supported. The paper reports pruning time and parameter count, but not actual wall-clock inference speed, memory bandwidth effects, kernel support, or end-to-end serving performance after structural changes.

Some technical discussion is questionable or confusing, including the degree-of-freedom comparison for Ridge versus RCPU and the claim that per-layer SVD cost is comparable to SparseGPT-style pruning; these need more careful justification.
The writing and presentation contain rough spots, formatting issues, and speculative explanations for benchmark behavior that are not backed by analysis.

strengths: The paper proposes a simple and technically well-motivated post-pruning compensation method: formulate structured column-pruning recovery as an Orthogonal Procrustes problem and update retained weights with an orthogonal transformation. This is elegant, closed-form, and plausibly more stable than unconstrained least-squares fitting on small calibration sets.

The method is practical: it requires no retraining, no architectural changes beyond the structured pruning already being performed, and has a clear implementation path for targeted projection matrices.

Empirical results are consistently positive across Llama-7B, Llama-2-13B, and additional Vicuna-7B appendix experiments. RCPU generally improves perplexity and downstream zero-shot accuracy over Wanda-sp and FLAP, especially at higher pruning ratios.

The paper includes useful ablations comparing rotation-only vs rotation-plus-scale, compensation targets, calibration sizes, and LS/Ridge alternatives. These analyses support the central claim that constrained updates can generalize better than less constrained compensation.
The presentation is mostly clear, with a clean problem formulation and understandable geometric intuition.
weaknesses: The novelty is meaningful but somewhat incremental. Orthogonal Procrustes is classical, and rotations/orthogonal transformations have already been explored in LLM pruning contexts such as SliceGPT and related rotated-space pruning methods. The main contribution is a useful adaptation rather than a major conceptual leap.

The baseline set is limited for a top-tier pruning paper. SliceGPT is only compared on Llama-2-13B downstream tasks, and there is no broad comparison to stronger or more recent structured pruning methods, mixed pruning schemes, or retraining/fine-tuning recovery baselines.

The evaluation scope is still narrow: only Llama-family dense decoder models, pruning ratios up to 30%, mostly WikiText-2 perplexity and standard zero-shot tasks. It is unclear whether the method transfers to larger models, newer architectures, multilingual/code models, or instruction-tuned/chat deployment settings beyond the limited Vicuna appendix.

The calibration/evaluation protocol needs clarification. The paper says WikiText-2 is used as calibration data and also reports WikiText-2 perplexity; without a precise split description, there is a concern that PPL evaluation may be partially coupled to the calibration distribution.

Efficiency claims are underdeveloped. The method reports pruning time and model size, but not realized end-to-end inference latency, throughput, memory bandwidth effects, or hardware-specific speedups after structured removal. These are central for a deployment-oriented pruning paper.

Reproducibility is incomplete. The code availability line appears blank, and important details such as exact calibration split, random seeds, evaluation harness settings, pruning implementation details across coupled projections, and statistical variability are insufficiently specified.

Some claims are stronger than the evidence. For example, explanations about why HellaSwag/WinoGrande benefit or why SliceGPT degrades at high pruning ratios are plausible but speculative without direct representational or distribution-shift analysis.
